reference: Her trainer wishes his pads were a bit thicker.
sk: Tréner by si prial, aby jeho lapy boli trochu hrubšie.
cz: Trenér by si přál, aby jeho lapy byly trochu tlustší.
acceptable: {Her|The} {trainer|coach} wishes his {pads|mitts|focus pads|focus mitts} were {a bit|a little|slightly} thicker.
{Her|The} {trainer|coach} wishes that his {pads|mitts} were {a bit|a little|slightly} thicker.

mistakes.text: {Her|The} trainer wishes his pads are {a bit|a little} thicker.
mistakes.feedback_sk: Po „wish“ o prítomnosti patrí minulý tvar: „were“, nie „are“.
mistakes.feedback_cz: Po „wish“ o přítomnosti patří minulý tvar: „were“, ne „are“.
mistakes.feedback_en: After “wish” about the present use a past form: “were”, not “are”.

mistakes.text: {Her|The} trainer wishes his pads would be {a bit|a little} thicker.
mistakes.feedback_sk: „Wish + would“ je pre zmenu správania. Pri stave je prirodzenejšie „were“.
mistakes.feedback_cz: „Wish + would“ je pro změnu chování. U stavu je přirozenější „were“.
mistakes.feedback_en: “Wish + would” is for changes in behaviour; for a state, “were” is more natural.

mistakes.text: {Her|The} trainer wish his pads were {a bit|a little} thicker.
mistakes.feedback_en: With “trainer” (he) the Present Simple form is “wishes”.

mistakes.text: {Her|The} trainer would wish that his pads were {a bit|a little} thicker.
mistakes.feedback_sk: „Would wish“ znie neprirodzene. Stačí „wishes“: „The trainer wishes his pads were…“.
mistakes.feedback_cz: „Would wish“ zní nepřirozeně. Stačí „wishes“: „The trainer wishes his pads were…“.

mistakes.text: {Her|The} trainer would like his pads to be {a bit|a little} thicker.
mistakes.feedback_sk: Význam sedí, no cvičí sa „wish“ + minulý tvar: „wishes his pads were“.
mistakes.feedback_cz: Význam sedí, ale procvičuje se „wish“ + minulý tvar: „wishes his pads were“.
mistakes.feedback_en: Same meaning, but this exercise practises “wish” + past form: “wishes his pads were”.

mistakes.text: {Her|The} trainer wishes his pads were {a bit|a little} more thick.

source_issues: Slovak/Czech have no possessive for the trainer and use 'by si prial/přál' (would like); 'The trainer' is accepted too.
